 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Vinicius Junior has offered a remarkably candid assessment of his recent performances for both Real Madrid and the Brazilian national team. The 26-year-old forward admitted that a combination of post-World Cup exhaustion and off-field distractions contributed to a slower start to the current campaign.
 The mental toll of the World Cup
 In a refreshing display of honesty, Vini has admitted that his preparation following the World Cup was not at the level required for his usual standards. The Brazilian international explained that the emotional weight of the tournament took a significant toll on his focus. The forward acknowledged that the pain of the early exit played a part in his decision to step away from the rigours of elite training during his time off.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I believe that I did not prepare myself better after the World Cup, because the impact of the World Cup is very large for all of us Brazilians. Losing so early was something we did not expect. So, I took the holidays to really enjoy, rest, distract myself and stay more with my family. I ended up training less than I trained in recent years," Vini said, as cited by Globo Esporte .
 Chasing the shadows of Messi and Ronaldo
 Vini has opened up on the immense pressure of staying at the pinnacle of world football, pointing to the extraterrestrial longevity of Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo as the ultimate—yet nearly impossible—benchmark. For a player who continues to define the highest echelons of the sport at 26 years of age, the Brazilian superstar is acutely aware of the stratospheric standards required to dominate year after year.
 "Maintaining such a high level for so long is always very difficult. I believe only Cristiano Ronaldo and Messi have managed to maintain it for so many years, achieving the same numbers. I'm human, I make mistakes often, but I always try to improve. I try to understand more about football, about the day-to-day, but I'm 26 years old and I have to enjoy life a little too," he explained during the press conference.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Market distractions and contract talk
 The Madrid star has candidly admitted that a whirlwind summer of transfer speculation and a tense contract renewal saga took a severe toll on his mental well-being. With European heavyweights circling for his signature and his future at the Santiago Bernabeu hanging in the balance, the striker revealed that the intense off-field distractions heavily disrupted his focus heading into the new campaign.
 "This perhaps affected my start to the season. Also about my renewal, about so many clubs having approached me last summer, it messed with my head a lot, as well as the situation at Real Madrid. But the season is very long," the star noted.
 Promises explosive Real Madrid comeback
 Despite the slow start, Vini remains optimistic about his ability to turn the tide. He pointed toward his history of slow starts followed by explosive finishes as proof that his best form is just around the corner. By identifying his shortcomings early, he hopes to recalibrate his focus for the business end of the season where he traditionally thrives for Los Blancos.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Last season, until December, I had only scored five goals. Then, I finished with more than 20 goals, as in all other seasons. I believe I am preparing, evolving, because, in the most decisive moment of the season, I am always there," he asserted confidently.
